That is a real mismatch, though line 24 makes the role hand back instead of working around the limit, and this CLI-only repo has no production service, so P1 is overstated.

The unanswerable group is diagnostic only. This is a one-line documentation error, so P3 fits better.

The tech-spec table at 02-tech-spec.md:264-268 sums to 13, plus 1 for the INV annotation and 2 for ADR 0002/0003 (line 270) makes 16, above the 01-scope.md:69 maximum of 15, and the spec still says 'Fits the cap; no re-split needed'. The ADR edits were disclosed and made at the Orchestrator's instruction, so this is an accounting and process lapse, not a hidden one.

STATE.md:24 marks Post-Launch 'done', but 03-close-out.md:3 and :33 say Post-Launch did not run by the owner's decision, and STATE.md:22-23 already use 'not run — owner's decision' for Security and Release. It is a status inconsistency with no safety effect, so P3 fits better.

SUPPORT_REPLIES.md:41 says the owner told the support session directly ('remove it') and labels the reply 'Data only', not an approval. The deletion removes a permissive rule, and the repo keeps S6 unresolved: 15-close-out.md:174 (T9a) requires the owner's disposition in the driving session, and 13-release-checklist-tier3.md:48 flags that no driving-session record exists. The remedy the finding asks for is already in place.

HANDOFF_CHECK.md:16 limits the validator to mechanical envelope checks and :58-60 says it never judges quality. No rule is contradicted or left unenforced; a fooled validator only lets an incomplete handoff through to downstream gates. The missing untrusted-input wording is a hardening suggestion, not a defect, and P1 is unsupported.

tests/test_judge_seen_skill.py:199-200 compares the freshly derived key/key.toml byte for byte with the committed one. CURRENT_MVP_STATUS.md:92-94 confirms the committed key gained rows after the freeze, so `test_sample_derivation_reproducible` fails even when derivation is correct. The repo records it as a known failure that 'a later slice must change'.

RUN_ECONOMICS.md:171-173 calls a 'timeout with no output' an infrastructure interruption that does not consume the retry budget. FAILURE_LOOP.md:10-21 says a stage attempt exceeding its wall-clock budget is a failure that counts against retries, and :65 has a `timeout` category, so the two protocols contradict. Nothing bounds repeated timed-out respawns, which undercuts non-negotiable rule 3.

The finding cuts the quoted sentence at the ellipsis. The full line (06-release-checklist.md:108) reads 'Any end-to-end figure … on held-out data, and any fifth-set result. I report none', so it excludes only held-out and fifth-set figures. The seen-set end-to-end figures in 03-implementation.md:14-19 are not contradicted, and line 102 labels seen-set results 'diagnostic'.

security-privacy.md:4 gives Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, and the file has no write-scope-guard hook, although the other artefact-only roles do (for example orchestrator.md:9-12). Line 62 says the role does not own code changes. The other Bash-holding roles I checked also have no hook, and a path-matching hook would not constrain Bash anyway, so P1 overstates it; P2 fits.

The per-fold re-selection is what the sweep calls its 'committed procedure' (02-baseline-sweep.py:349-350). 02-baseline.md:43 says 'LOSO procedure as in the brief (max of min(Bar1, Bar2) on the other three sets)'. 01-scope.md:65 does say 'single chosen setting', so the wording is loose. The outcome does not change, because 02-tech-spec.md:23-25 shows no cell reaches 80% on both bars pooled.

__main__.py:56 echoes result.question verbatim, and retrieve (search.py:457) only rejects empty or wordless questions. A multi-line question can therefore put 'no confident match' or 'Deciding signal:' at line start in retrieve output, which breaks the literal wording of SAFETY_INVARIANTS.md:62-64. The only source of the injected text is the operator's own input, and the program itself never emits a verdict, so P3 or a narrowed invariant is enough.

APPROVAL_PROTOCOL.md:47-48 says 'Denied → stop the slice' but gives no status transition, and step 2 (line 28) leaves the slice at blocked-on-approval. SLICE_STATE.md:33 allows only in-progress, blocked-on-approval, blocked-on-failure and done, so a denied slice has no terminal state.
